goal: The claim store refuses to acquire an item that shares a conflict_key with a different live claim, so two conflicting items never hold concurrent claims, and the refusal clears when the conflicting claim is released or swept.

relevant: .flywheel/specs/00049-distributed-scheduling-metadata.md -- acceptance criteria #8, #9, #10, #13 (conflict part), #15, #17 and decisions D-3, D-4, D-5 this task satisfies

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims.py -- the ClaimStore protocol and SqliteClaimStore.acquire_claim (~line 427): supply each item's conflict keys at acquire time and refuse on overlap with a different live claim
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims_postgres.py -- mirror the same exclusion on the Postgres backend
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_orchestrator_claims.py -- keep this suite green; it pins acquire/renew/release/list on both backends (the v1 sentinel, expiry-steal, same-worker re-acquire)
constraints: Conflict keys are supplied to the claim store at acquire time (D-4), so exclusion does not depend on work_items being freshly synced. Refuse the acquire (return no claim) when a DIFFERENT live claim holds an overlapping conflict key; a same-worker re-acquire of its own task still succeeds (existing behavior).
The refusal must clear when the conflicting claim is released or its lease lapses and it is swept -- a previously-refused item becomes acquirable again.

If enforcing exclusion requires persisting conflict keys on a claim, add the column additively and bump orchestrator_schema_version additively: a pre-existing store (holding task_claims and work_items rows) opened by the new code MUST keep every row and converge -- no drop-and-recreate, no hard version-mismatch error (mirrors 00048 criterion #9).
The behavior holds on BOTH the SQLite and Postgres claim-store backends.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do NOT block or queue-until-clear -- exclusion is refuse-and-skip; the worker falls through to the next ready item (the already-shipped 'claim fails -> try next' fallback) (D-3).
Do NOT enforce conflict in the scheduler / ready_set -- the claim store is the single cross-worker mutual-exclusion point.
Do NOT alter acquire/renew/release/list semantics for non-conflicting claims, including the lease/version bump on an ordinary claim (#17).
Do NOT perform a destructive migration or raise a hard version mismatch on the additive bump (#15).
Do NOT modify flywheel-core; do NOT modify files under tests/ or weaken existing claim assertions.
edge_cases: A (conflict_keys {"k"}) claimed by worker-1, then B (conflict_keys {"k"}) attempted by worker-2: B is refused while A stays live and owned by worker-1; after A is released, B becomes acquirable.
A (conflict_keys {"k1"}) and B (conflict_keys {"k2"} or {}) can hold concurrent live claims -- exclusion fires only on actual key overlap, never on any second concurrent claim.
A worker re-acquiring its own already-held task must still succeed with the version bump intact.
